---
title: "What should I do when some measurements are NA?"
---

## The question

What should I do when some measurements are NA?

## What to check and do

1. Count missing values. 2. Check why they are missing. 3. Report how many observations the calculation uses and apply a justified missing-data rule.

## Worked example: airquality

This example uses a public dataset distributed with R. It does not make claims about observations outside that dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("airquality")
answer <- ru_apply("missing_values", data=d, x="Ozone")
stopifnot(answer["missing"]>0, answer["available"]<answer["total"])
```

The reported mean uses available ozone observations only. Dropping observations is not automatically unbiased when missingness is systematic.

## Apply the method to another question

Replace the data frame and column names with those in your own file:

```r
ru_apply("missing_values", data=your_data, x="measurement_column")
```

For relationships between two columns, exclude or model missing pairs jointly rather than deleting NA values independently from each variable.


## Inspect conditions

Use `ru_plan("missing_values")` for available-versus-missing input routes. A calculation can run even when its assumptions do not justify an inference.
